tagline: What fire does to good meat.
sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.
typography: A bold, warm display face for dish names and the end card, set large and immediate, paired with a sturdy sans for the one-line description and price. The type has to carry over fire behind it: confident, appetite-first, never a restrained editorial serif.
voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.
